narrative.overview:
Every page is a set of numbered engineering sheets, issued for construction. The ground is Prussian-blue cyanotype with a two-level drafting grid. Content sits inside framed sheets (a heavy white border with a thin dim outline offset outside it), and each sheet is listed on a fixed index rail at the right edge. Systems aren't described, they're drawn: architecture schematics, dimension lines, section hatching, a staircase elevation for education. Line work plots itself in with scroll progress, so reading the page is watching the set get drafted.

Colour is the material, not decoration. Everything is ink on blueprint: bright line-white for anything that matters, dim blue-white for labels and construction marks, faint grid lines for structure. One red approval stamp is the only warm colour. It marks the action the visitor should take next ("View experience", "Start a project") and the key moments in the process (Prototype, Deploy). Photographs are printed onto the blueprint (grayscale, screen-blended) and develop into full colour when hovered.

Type is drafting lettering: Barlow Condensed in uppercase for everything structural, from the 140px hero name to 11px title-block labels, with Barlow (regular width) for readable specification notes. The system is flat and square; depth comes from double rules, outlines and inversion, never shadow.
keyCharacteristics: Prussian-blue cyanotype ground with a 32px minor / 160px major drafting grid
White line work that plots in with scroll (stroke-dashoffset driven by a --p progress variable)
Framed, numbered sheets plus a fixed sheet-index rail
Barlow Condensed uppercase at every structural level; Barlow for prose
One red approval stamp, rotated −3°, rationed to the next action
Square corners and no shadows; circles only for nodes and markers

rules.name: The One Stamp Rule
rules.body: Stamp Red appears on the primary action and on no more than two marked process nodes per view. It's an approval mark: if two stamps compete on one screen, one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The Ink Hierarchy Rule
rules.body: Importance is expressed by line weight and brightness, not by hue: Line White for content, Line Dim for annotation, Line Faint for structure. Never introduce a second blue for emphasis.

rules.name: The Lettering Rule
rules.body: Headings, labels, navigation, buttons, tags and drawing annotations are uppercase Barlow Condensed. Prose (descriptions, notes, the core-focus paragraph) is sentence-case Barlow. Never set prose in the condensed face.

rules.name: The Numbers Rule
rules.body: Years, counts and stats use font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums, so values that animate or align in columns don't jitter.

rules.name: The Sheet Rule
rules.body: Every top-level section is a framed sheet registered on the rail, with an id and a title. New pages are new drawing sets; new sections are new sheets, never unframed bands.

rules.name: The Drawing-Over-Description Rule
rules.body: Where a system, process or progression can be drawn (architecture, pipeline, timeline, growth), draw it as scroll-plotted line work and let the prose annotate it.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Paper doesn't cast shadows on a blueprint. To raise something, frame it, double its rule or invert it.

dos: Do wrap every drawing-set page in <main className="dh"> and build it from components/blueprint (Sheet, SheetRail, TopBar, DrawingFooter, useDrawingScroll). Add the route to DRAWING_ROUTES in App.tsx so the legacy header and footer step aside.
Do frame every top-level section as a sheet with an id and a rail title.
Do draw systems, pipelines and timelines as scroll-plotted SVG line work, annotated in condensed caps.
Do use Stamp Red only for the primary action and marked key nodes, one stamp per view.
Do express hierarchy with line weight and brightness: Line White, then Line Dim, then Line Faint.
Do put labels that sit on lines or hatching on a Ground knockout so they stay legible.
Do print photographs onto the blueprint (grayscale, screen blend) and develop them to colour on hover.
Do use the dashed 2px Line White focus outline on every interactive element.
Do keep a still state for reduced motion that still reads as a finished drawing.
donts: Don't add box-shadows, glows, rounded corners or pills. Circles are for nodes and markers only.
Don't add a second accent, a second blue, or gradients beyond the drafting grid.
Don't set prose in Barlow Condensed or headings in Barlow.
Don't use a weight that isn't in the font request (Barlow Condensed 400–700, Barlow 400–600).
Don't let any text use Line Faint, and don't use Line Dim for body-length copy below 15px.
Don't use the retired Swiss tokens (Inter, swissRed, paper #FAFAFA, the 40px drifting grid) on any converted page.
